notes.title: Notice the order
notes.text: In Matthew, Jesus questions the disciples before calming the storm (8:26). In Mark and Luke, the question about faith follows the calming (Mark 4:39–40; Luke 8:24–25). This is an observation about these passages; it does not by itself establish how they were composed.

notes.title: A question about understanding
notes.text: Dale B. Martin reads Mark’s disciples’ question about Jesus in 4:41 within a wider narrative pattern: the disciples struggle to understand him. This is Martin’s literary interpretation, not a claim that this scene independently establishes what the historical disciples knew.

notes.title: From comparison to interpretation
notes.text: Martin describes redaction criticism as studying how an author edits source material to communicate a message. That method depends on an argued account of the sources. Here, the alignment helps you notice the texts before choosing a theory about their relationship.
